trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers (miners/validators) produce blocks that must be validated against consensus rules before acceptance. Malicious block producers may attempt to create invalid blocks to exploit validation bugs or force chain splits.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Entity producing blocks that trigger fork activation when threshold is reached

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers propagate blocks via P2P protocol. All received blocks must pass full validation before acceptance regardless of peer reputation.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Remote node propagating blocks via P2P network

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Message callers (EOAs or contracts) initiate EVM execution with arbitrary code and data. The EVM must validate all inputs including depth limits, gas constraints, and code restrictions.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Entity initiating the message call (EOA or contract)

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers in the discovery protocol exchange ENR records and ping/pong messages. ENR signatures must be cryptographically verified before trusting peer information.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: External Ethereum node requesting ENR information via discovery protocol

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly marked as untrusted - may send malicious ENRRequests for amplification attacks. Ping exchange requirement provides rate limiting protection.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: External entity sending potentially malicious ENRRequest for amplification attack

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction sources (users via RPC, peers via P2P) submit transaction bytes that must be fully decoded, validated, and have signatures verified before acceptance.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: External source of transactions (user via RPC, peer via P2P)

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction signers are authenticated via SECP256K1 signature verification. While the signature proves the signer authorized the transaction, the transaction content itself still requires validation (nonce, gas, etc.).
trusted_external_entities.original_description: External entity that created the transaction signature

security_assumptions: Block must pass full consensus validation
Fork rules applied based on block height
Invalid blocks rejected regardless of peer
Expiration timestamp must be valid (future)
Prior ping exchange required (amplification protection)
Response includes signed ENR with cryptographic proof
ENR sequence comparison used to detect stale records
Pong response includes local enr-seq for bidirectional update
Request hash must match pending ENRRequest
ENR signature must be cryptographically valid
Only validated ENRs stored in node table
Ping history check prevents amplification attacks
Expiration timestamp prevents replay attacks
No response sent to unauthorized requesters
Transaction must be successfully decoded
Signature must be valid and recover sender
Gas, nonce, and init code size validated
R and S values must be within SECP256K1 curve parameters
ECDSA recovery must successfully extract public key
Sender address derived from verified signature
